paper_title: Eine neue Orientierung für den Mindestlohn
caption: Nominaler Mindestlohn, Verbraucherpreise und allgemeines Lohnniveaus, 2015-2025
model_annotation: The graph displays the trends of four different economic indicators over time, from January 2015 to January 2025. The x-axis represents time, marked at regular intervals from January 2015 to January 2025, with labels at every other year. The y-axis represents an index value, ranging from 80 to 160, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The graph compares the trends of Mindestlohn (minimum wage), HVPI (consumer price index), Bruttostundenlöhne und -gehälter (gross hourly wages and salaries), and their adjusted values. The Mindestlohn is represented by a maroon line, starting at around 100 in January 2015, remaining relatively stable until mid-2017, and then increasing to around 114 in January 2022, with a significant jump to around 140 in January 2023, and continuing to rise to around 150 in January 2025. The HVPI is depicted as a light green line, beginning at 100 in January 2015, increasing gradually to around 105 in mid-2017, and then rising to around 115 in January 2022, with a further increase to around 125 in January 2023, and reaching around 130 in January 2025. The Bruttostundenlöhne und -gehälter is shown as a light blue line, starting at 100 in January 2015 and steadily increasing to around 125 in January 2022, with a notable jump to around 140 in January 2023, and continuing to rise to around 155 in January 2025. The adjusted HVPI and Bruttostundenlöhne und -gehälter, represented by dark green and dark blue lines respectively, remain relatively stable around 100 until January 2023, after which they exhibit a similar trend to their non-adjusted counterparts, with the dark blue line reaching around 155 in January 2025.
